rv.q: The wave of euphoria "Falsettos" evokes is inseparable from the wave of tears that rises audibly through the house once Mr. Finn raises the ghosts of those Falsettoland loved ones no longer here to join the party.
Finn brilliantly uses musical comedy to explore what constitutes a family, while humanizing the extensive tragedy of the AIDS epidemic.
The time has never been riper for a revival of this beautiful show.
The cast is a thoroughly winsome one, which compensates for the first act becoming at points a bit repetitious once the basic situation is set.

cn.t: This humane musical comedy brilliantly explores family and the AIDS crisis with playful wit and emotional depth. The second act delivers a powerful punch, elevated by top-flight performances and expert direction.

vs.sum: The John Golden Theatre offers good sightlines from most seats, though sound quality can vary, especially under the mezzanine. Seating comfort is typical of older theaters with tight legroom, but the venue maintains a pleasant ambiance overall. Facilities are adequate, though not exceptional.

acc.note: 5 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. No wheelchair-accessible restroom (use adjacent Schoenfeld).
